A **test case** is a sequence of **keyword** calls, one per line. Each keyword
is an action — `Log`, `Should Be Equal`, `Open Browser` — with optional
arguments after it. Read top to bottom, a good test reads like a procedure.

Keywords come from three places: the **built-in** library (always available),
**standard and third-party libraries** you import, and **user keywords** you
write yourself. You will use all three in this part.

Test cases live in **suite files** — `.robot` files. A folder of suite files is
itself a suite (a *directory suite*), which lets you group related tests and
give the whole group shared setup. You will meet directory suites in Chapter 6.

```diagram
tree "How .robot files and folders form suites"
node tests/ #folder -- directory suite {
  node __init__.robot :muted :dashed -- shared settings · setup / teardown
  node login.robot #file -- file suite
  node api/ #folder -- directory suite {
    node smoke.robot #file -- file suite
    node crud.robot #file -- file suite
  }
}
legend :solid "a suite"
legend :dashed :muted "initializer (not a suite itself)"
```

Robot Framework is open source under the **Apache License 2.0**, stewarded by
the non-profit **Robot Framework Foundation**. The canonical home for docs,
libraries, and the community is the project website.
